title: Mutexes, Semaphores and Abandonment
summary: Exclusive access across processes with a named mutex - ownership, recursion, releasing, and WAIT_ABANDONED when the owner died holding it - and semaphores for limiting how many can do something at once.

cards.q: What does WAIT_ABANDONED mean on a mutex wait?
cards.a: The caller now owns the mutex, but its previous owner ended while holding it, so the protected data may be inconsistent.

cards.q: Why is a Win32 mutex called recursive?
cards.a: The owning thread can wait on it again without blocking, releasing it once per successful wait.

cards.q: Why is there no abandonment for semaphores?
cards.a: A semaphore has no owner; any thread may release it, so Windows cannot know who should have.

cards.q: A semaphore created with initial count 4 and maximum 4 has five waiters. How many get through at once?
cards.a: Four; the fifth waits until one releases.
